messages:
sara (support): Hi team — Customer Acme Health on Redwood Private reports control plane registration failing from their VPC since this morning after a firewall change. Errors: repeated mTLS handshake resets and 'TLS alert: handshake failure' in client logs. They can reach the control plane IP but the TLS session never completes.
sara (support): Attaching what's been shared so far: tcpdump from customer and the partial openssl output. Asking for quick repro pointers and whether we need to whitelist anything on their FW.
lee (acme-netops): We flipped an inspection policy at 08:12 and started seeing failures at ~08:15. Logs show src=10.12.0.45:49152 -> 3.120.45.98:443, action=drop, reason=ssl-inspect-failure. We can share pcap.
sara (support): Thanks @lee — can you paste the openssl s_client output you got? Also did you see any ClientHello payload or was it truncated?
lee (acme-netops): Here — ran from a host in the VPC:
```
openssl s_client -connect controlplane.private.redwood.example:443 -servername controlplane.private.redwood.example -alpn h2
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
write:errno=104
139744827512896:error:0A00018E:SSL routines:tls_process_server_hello:unsupported protocol:../ssl/statem/statem_lib.c:197
---
no peer certificate
No client certificate CA names sent
---
```
It seems to fail quickly; tcpdump shows ClientHello then RST from an intermediate appliance.
dan (eng-infra): This pattern often means active TLS inspection is terminating the handshake. Two things to check: 1) Is SNI being rewritten or stripped by their proxy? 2) Are TLS record sizes being clamped/truncated causing the server to abort?
dan (eng-infra): Can you run a raw tcpdump and extract the TLS ClientHello bytes length? Command we ask customers to run: `sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/hello.pcap host 3.120.45.98 and port 443` and then share the pcap. Also try `curl -v --http2 -H 'Host: controlplane.private.redwood.example' https://3.120.45.98/` to see if SNI/no-SNI changes behavior.
lee (acme-netops): Uploaded pcap to our S3 link. Quick grep shows ClientHello size 1024 bytes, then appliance sends TCP RST after 150ms.
matt (sre): If the inspection appliance sees a large ClientHello (with many supported groups and keyshares for TLS1.3) some middleboxes choke and reset. We should advise customer to either disable TLS inspection for control plane IPs or configure passthrough.
matt (sre): Also ask them to test forcing TLS1.2 to see if TLS1.3 keyshare size is the culprit: `openssl s_client -connect 3.120.45.98:443 -tls1_2 -servername controlplane.private.redwood.example`
lee (acme-netops): I ran TLS1.2 and it connected (handshake completed). So TLS1.3 ClientHello seems to trigger the drop.
dan (eng-infra): That confirms middlebox incompatibility with TLS1.3 extensions/keyshare length. Two mitigation paths: 1) Have Acme allow direct pass-through for our control plane IPs and port 443 (recommended). 2) On our side we can offer they pin to a TLS1.2 fallback (temporary), but that reduces forward secrecy properties.
sara (support): Customer asked for exact firewall rule examples and whether we need to whitelist any FQDNs or IP ranges.
matt (sre): Provide them the CIDR list used by Private control plane in their region: 3.120.45.96/28 and 3.120.46.0/24 (example). Recommend allowing outbound TCP 443 to those ranges with no SSL-inspect. For Palo Alto, a suggested bypass policy:
```
# PANOS example
set rulebase security rules "redwood-controlplane-bypass" from trust to untrust source 10.12.0.0/16 destination 3.120.45.96/28 application service-https action allow log-start yes log-end yes
set rulebase security rules "redwood-controlplane-bypass" profile-setting types ssl-decrypt-settings-decrypt-mode no-decrypt
```
For F5: create a passthrough virtual server for destination IPs and disable client-side SSL profile.
sara (support): Also note: if customers can't disable inspect, recommend enabling SNI passthrough/transparent TLS flow or reducing ClientHello extension set (not always possible).
dan (eng-infra): Escalating to product infra to see whether we should publish a KB about TL S inspection incompatibility and region IP CIDRs. Tagging @deploy-bot to record the incident ticket.
deploy-bot: Incident ticket INF-2024-792 created and linked to support case S-84721.
lee (acme-netops): We'll request a firewall policy change to bypass SSL inspect for the given CIDRs and report back. Any quick tests to confirm on our side?
matt (sre): After applying bypass, test again with TLS1.3 openssl: `openssl s_client -connect controlplane.private.redwood.example:443 -servername controlplane.private.redwood.example -alpn h2` and confirm no RST and that server sends Certificate. Also validate connection from multiple subnets if they have asymmetrical egress NAT.
sara (support): Action items: 1) Acme to add bypass policy and re-test (lee). 2) Support to collect post-change captures and logs (sara). 3) EngInfra to draft KB + update region CIDRs if needed (dan). 4) SRE to monitor for rollout impact (matt).
sara (support): Closing loop: if bypass isn't possible, we'll coordinate a temporary TLS1.2 compatibility workaround and escalate for longer-term product guidance on exposing smaller ClientHello footprints. Thanks all :thumbsup:
